dedupe.result: Neither paper was in the completed ledger. The helicon DOI was present only as a blocked retry candidate; it was promoted after an open author manuscript became available and passed full-text validation. The foam-shock paper is a distinct formal HPLSE record.

retry_recovery.result: The legal author manuscript passed PDF and text validation, was analyzed and entered in the completed ledger; its retry record was removed.

skipped_candidates.reason: A theory paper on nonuniform hydrodynamic plasma-wave instability in a gated InGaAs/GaAs electron channel was materially less aligned with the repository's laser-plasma, HEDP, PIC and beam-application priorities.

No newly accessible non-duplicate record closed the full laser-accelerated beam to converter or catcher to gamma, neutron or activation to dose or shielding chain, so no adjacent-topic paper was used as a substitute.

evidence_boundary: Lestz et al. directly measure modulated electron-temperature response, MSE-constrained equilibrium changes and sawtooth timing, while the quoted 20 ± 10 kA helicon component is a residual after subtracting modeled Ohmic, bootstrap, neutral-beam and EC-driven currents; one-sided antenna operation prevents a propagation-direction reversal test, and the low-beta L-mode proof-of-principle does not establish reactor efficiency. Turianska et al. directly image pusher and shock evolution and robustly infer a pusher velocity, while effective laser intensity and megabar pressure are hydrodynamic-model inferences; homogeneous-foam MULTI and FLASH results do not validate directly irradiated undercritical-foam microphysics. No GENRAY, TRANSP, EFIT, MULTI, FLASH or raw diagnostic analysis was rerun locally.
